title: NADH-linked microtiter plate-based assay for measuring Rubisco activity
author: Cristina Rodrigues Gabriel Sales
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf9rjr56
materials: REAGENTS & SOLUTIONS TO PREPARE BEFOREHAND Powder chemical stocks stored at -20°C: let warm up to room temperature on desiccant before opening container. Expensive chemicals purchased in very small amounts (mg), for which concentration in assay is not critical (e.g. in excess): trust quantity stated by the supplier and add ultrapure H 2 O / solvent to container for final concentration (e.g. 2,3-dPGA). Protein and substrate solutions should typically be stored at -80°C. Freeze proteins in LN 2 before storing at -80°C. Store in small aliquots to prevent multiple freeze-thaw cycles. If using in consecutive days, protein solutions can be kept at 4°C. Buffers and solutions will last longer if filtered through 0.22 µm membrane.
SOLUTIONS TO PREPARE JUST BEFORE USE Prepared with reagents/solutions described in step 1.

START Thaw the frozen solutions that will be used in the day. Prepare CO 2 -free ultrapure H 2 O by bubbling with nitrogen (5 min/100 mL). Turn on the microplate reader and set up for the temperature that Rubisco activity will be performed, select kinetic protocol at 340 nm. The temperature to be used for the Rubisco activity measurement depends on the experiment goals. Typical measurement temperatures are 25 °C (standard) and 30 °C , depending on the species. Assays can be performed at a range of temperatures, however high temperatures might lead to evaporation of the assay mix and, since rates will be faster, the assay might become less sensitive. Turn on the centrifuge and set to 4 °C . Collect samples from -80 °C into liquid nitrogen container. Prepare the complete extraction buffer (from step 3.1) and the complete assay buffer (from step 3.2) and keep it On ice .

steps.title: Prepare Basic Extraction Buffer (1x)
steps.instruction: Prepare a buffer containing 50 mM Bicine-NaOH (pH 8.2), 20 mM MgCl2.6H2O, 1 mM EDTA, 2 mM Benzamidine, and 5 mM ε-Aminocaproic acid.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve components in ultrapure H2O and adjust pH to 8.2 with NaOH.
Degas the solution by bubbling with nitrogen (5 min/100 mL).
Add 50 mM 2-Mercaptoethanol.
Adjust for final volume and dispense in aliquots (e.g., 50 mL Falcon tubes).
Store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Additional Stock Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the following stock solutions for extraction and assay buffers:

substeps.instruction: 1 M DTT: Dissolve in ultrapure H2O; store at 4 °C.
100 mM PMSF: Dissolve in ethanol 99%; store at 4 °C.
20 mM RuBP (≥99% purity): Store at -20 °C.
1 M Bicine-NaOH (pH 8): Dissolve in ultrapure H2O, adjust pH to 8.2 with NaOH, filter through 0.22 µm membrane; store at 4 °C.
1 M MgCl2.6H2O: Dissolve in ultrapure H2O, filter through 0.22 µm membrane; store at 4 °C.
0.5 M NaHCO3: Dissolve in ultrapure H2O, filter through 0.22 µm membrane; store at 4 °C.
3 M KCl: Dissolve in ultrapure H2O, filter through 0.22 µm membrane; store at 4 °C.
0.1 M 2,3-dPGA: Dissolve solid with ultrapure H2O, aliquot; store at -80 °C.
0.5 M ADP: Add powder to tube, dissolve with ultrapure H2O, add 4 M NaOH (~10 µL/mL) to approx. pH 7, add ultrapure H2O to final volume, aliquot; store at -80 °C.
14 mM NADH: Dissolve in 100 M Bicine-NaOH pH 8, aliquot, and protect from light; store at -80 °C.
36 U/ml Enolase: Dissolve solid with 100 M Bicine-NaOH pH 8, aliquot; store at -80 °C.
PK/LDH (1 KU/ml PK + 1.4 KU/ml LDH): Store at -20 °C.
3 KU/ml d-PGM: Store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Complete Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix the following components on ice:

substeps.instruction: Basic extraction buffer (1x)
10 mM DTT
1 mM PMSF
1% (v/v) Plant protease inhibitor cocktail

steps.title: Prepare Complete Assay Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the assay buffer and NADH mixture on ice, wrapped in aluminium foil to protect NADH from light.

substeps.instruction: Thaw assay buffer and NADH aliquots on ice.
Mix the required volumes of assay buffer and NADH (Example for 140 wells: 8722 µL assay buffer without NADH and 799.4 µL NADH).

steps.title: Set Up Microtiter Plate
steps.instruction: Prepare the 96-well microtiter plate before starting extraction.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 127 µL CO2-free ultrapure H2O into the blank well (singlet).
Pipette 121 µL CO2-free ultrapure H2O into sample wells (6 wells: triplicates for initial and triplicates for total activity).
Add 68 µL of complete assay buffer to each well.
Gently mix by pipetting up and down 5 times while stirring.
Add 6 µL of 20 mM RuBP to the wells designated for initial Rubisco activity.
Cover the plate to protect from light.

steps.title: Extract Rubisco
steps.instruction: Perform rapid extraction to prevent enzyme deactivation.

substeps.instruction: Add complete extraction buffer to an ice-cold mortar.
Add leaf sample from liquid nitrogen and grind thoroughly for 30 to 60 seconds.
Collect homogenate into an ice-cold 1.5 mL microtube.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 1 minute at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant into another ice-cold 1.5 mL microtube.

steps.title: Measure Rubisco Activity
steps.instruction: Perform the NADH-linked assay at 30 °C, monitoring absorbance at 340 nm.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µL of sample supernatant to the 'total activity' wells first, then to the 'initial activity' wells, mixing by pipetting up and down 10 times while stirring.
Immediately place the plate in the reader and monitor absorbance at 340 nm.
For initial activity: The reaction starts upon extract addition.
For total activity: Incubate for 3 minutes at 30 °C (to allow carbamylation), then pause reading and add 6 µL of 20 mM RuBP.
Resume monitoring absorbance until the reaction reaches a plateau.
